mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 jobs over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE is below 4.5% over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.0%) signals delayed monetary tightening, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction signal falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 600.0 thousand units, it signals strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 600.0 over the next 60 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a robust housing market and strong labor conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and PAYEMS rise.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, high consumer spending (RSAFS) signals potential overvaluation and impending slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansions when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average.
